record.title: Unbounded resistance conjecture for linear 2-trees of growing diameter
record.statement: Let $G$ be a linear 2-tree, and let its diameter tend to infinity. Let the maximal resistance distance of $G$ mean the maximum of $r_G(u,v)$ over pairs of vertices. **Unbounded resistance conjecture.** If the diameter of the linear 2-tree tends to infinity, then its maximal resistance distance is unbounded. The paper proves this for straight linear 2-trees and their connected subgraphs containing the two end vertices, while the assertion for arbitrary linear 2-trees is left as a conjecture.
record.source_name: Wayne Barrett, Emily J. Evans and Amanda E. Francis, “Resistance distance in straight linear 2-trees”, arXiv:1712.05883 (2017).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1712.05883

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of December 2017).

record.title: The third and fourth largest coset leader conjecture for odd-characteristic BCH codes
record.statement: Let $q$ be an odd prime power and let $n=q^m+1$, with the quantities $\delta_3$ and $\delta_4$ defined as in the preceding cases for even $m$. **Third and fourth largest coset leader conjecture.** If $\delta_3$ and $\delta_4$ are given as above, then $\delta_3$ and $\delta_4$ are the third and fourth largest coset leaders, respectively. These formulas are conjectured to hold uniformly based on the Magma computations described in the paper; the statement concerns the ordering of the largest $q$-cyclotomic coset leaders relevant to BCH codes, and no proof or resolution is supplied here.
record.source_name: Yang Liu, Ruihu Li, Luobin Guo and Hao Song, “Dimensions of nonbinary antiprimitive BCH codes and some conjectures”, arXiv:1712.06842 (2018).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1712.06842

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of December 2017).

record.title: Existence of extremal graphs for clique density
record.statement:
Let $\mathcal{G}(\Delta,\omega)$ be the class of graphs with maximum degree at most $\Delta$ and clique number at most $\omega$, and let $f_t(\Delta,\omega)$ be the supremum of $\rho_t(G)$ over this class. **Existence conjecture.** For all $t\geq 3$ and $3\leq\omega\leq\Delta+1$, there exists a graph $G\in\mathcal{G}(\Delta,\omega)$ such that

$$
\rho_t(G)=f_t(\Delta,\omega).
$$

The paper notes that its results do not establish attainment of the supremum for all relevant parameters; this conjecture asks for an extremal graph in every allowed case and remains open.
record.source_name: R. Kirsch and A. J. Radcliffe, “Maximizing the density of K_t's in graphs of bounded degree and clique number”, arXiv:1712.07769 (2020).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1712.07769

Status: **solved** according to the source (as of December 2017). “When restricting $\w(G)$ but not $\D(G)$, Zykov's Theorem shows that the same graphs maximize the number of cliques of every size.”

record.title: Li–Wu's lower-bound conjecture for conflict-free connection numbers of trees
record.statement:
Let $T$ be a tree of order $n$, and let $P_n$ be the path on $n$ vertices. Write $cfc(G)$ for the conflict-free connection number of a graph $G$. **Li–Wu's conjecture.** For every tree $T$ of order $n$,

$$
cfc(T)\geq cfc(P_n)=\lceil\log_{2} n\rceil.
$$

The conjecture asserts that among trees of a fixed order, the path minimizes the conflict-free connection number. The surrounding results determine this number for paths and several other tree classes, but the general lower bound is presented as a conjecture.
record.source_name: Hong Chang, Meng Ji, Xueliang Li and Jingshu Zhang, “Conflict-free connection of trees”, arXiv:1712.10010 (2018).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1712.10010

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of December 2017).

record.title: Three-dimensional maximum permanent conjecture for prescribed matrix sum
record.statement:
Let $\omega_n$ be the class of nonnegative row-substochastic matrices, let $\sigma(A)$ denote the sum of the entries of $A$, and write $\omega_n^s=\{A\in\omega_n:\sigma(A)=s\}$. For $A\in\omega_3$ with $2<\sigma(A)\leq3$, define

$$
F(s)=\max\{\operatorname{per}(I-A)\mid A\in\omega_3,\ \sigma(A)=s\}.
$$

**Three-dimensional maximum permanent conjecture.** With $\alpha=\frac{-3+\sqrt{57}}{2}$,

$$
F(s)=
\begin{cases}
\frac{s^2-5s+12}{4},&\alpha<s\leq3,\\
6-4s,&2<s\leq\alpha.
\end{cases}
$$

The preceding lemma only supplies lower bounds from two explicit matrices; equality with the displayed piecewise expression is conjectural, and the source gives no resolution.
record.source_name: Zhi Chen and Lei Cao, “On the maximum of the permanent of (I-A)”, arXiv:1801.00225 (2017).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1801.00225

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of January 2018).

record.title: The asymptotic conjecture for odd cycle-creating paths
record.statement:
Let $H(n,k)$ denote the maximum size of a family of paths in the complete graph $K_n$ such that the union of every pair contains a cycle of length $k$. The established cases include $H(n,2^{\ell}+1)=2^{n-o(n)}$ for every integer $\ell\geq 1$. **Odd-cycle path conjecture.** For every integer $k\geq 1$, 

$$
H(n,2k+1)=2^{n-o(n)}.
$$

This conjecture predicts that the exponential order established for odd cycle lengths of the form $2^{\ell}+1$ holds for every odd cycle length. The cited source is described as conjecturing analogous behaviour for other values of $k$; the general case is not resolved here.
record.source_name: Daniel Soltész, “Even cycle creating paths”, arXiv:1801.00737 (2018).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1801.00737

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of January 2018).

record.title: Conjecture that the exact induced density formula holds for all graph sizes
record.statement:
Let $H$ be a strongly asymmetric graph on $h$ vertices. Let $i_H(n)$ be the maximum number of induced copies of $H$ in an $n$-vertex graph, and let $g(n,h)$ be the recursively defined nested-blowup count. **Exact density conjecture.** For every $n\in\mathbb{N}$,

$$
i_H(n)=g(n,h).
$$

Consequently, the inducibility of $H$ satisfies

$$
i_H=\frac{h!}{h^h-h}.
$$

The preceding theorem establishes the formula only in the range covered there; this conjecture proposes its extension to all $n$ for strongly asymmetric graphs.
record.source_name: Raphael Yuster, “On the exact maximum induced density of almost all graphs and their inducibility”, arXiv:1801.01047 (2018).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1801.01047

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of January 2018).

record.title: Hähnle's monomial-family bound conjecture
record.statement:
Let $g(d,n)$ be the maximum number $t$ of pairwise-disjoint nonempty families $F_1,F_2,\dots,F_t$ of degree-$d$ monomials in $n$ variables satisfying: for every $1\le i<j<k\le t$, if $m_i\in F_i$ and $m_k\in F_k$, then some $m_j\in F_j$ is divisible by the greatest common divisor of $m_i$ and $m_k$. **Hähnle's conjecture.**

$$
g(d,n)\le d(n-1)+1.
$$

The source gives examples attaining equality. The status of this bound is not resolved in the supplied text.
record.source_name: Gil Kalai, “Three Puzzles on Mathematics, Computation, and Games”, arXiv:1801.02602 (2018).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1801.02602

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of January 2018).

record.title: Classification conjecture for symmetric universally self-predicting Boolean functions
record.statement:
A Boolean function is **symmetric** if its value depends only on the Hamming weight of its input; it is **universally self-predicting (USP)** if it is self-predicting for every admissible noise parameter. The **Majority** function outputs the sign of the sum of its input bits, and the **largest character** is the character associated with the largest nontrivial Fourier level.

**Symmetric USP-function conjecture.** The only symmetric USP functions are Majority and the largest character. In particular, Majority is the only monotone and symmetric USP function.

This conjecture seeks to characterize the symmetric members of the universally self-predicting class; the supplied text does not state a resolution.
record.source_name: Nir Weinberger and Ofer Shayevitz, “Self-Predicting Boolean Functions”, arXiv:1801.04103 (2019).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1801.04103

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of January 2018).

record.title: Kar–Nikolov's deficiency stabilisation conjecture
record.statement:
Let $G$) be a residually finite finitely presented group. For a finitely presented group $G$, its **deficiency** $\delta(G)$ is the maximum of $|X|-|R|$ over all presentations $G=\langle X\mid R\rangle$. **Kar–Nikolov's deficiency stabilisation conjecture.** If

$$
\delta(H)-1=[G:H](\delta(G)-1)
$$

for every finite-index subgroup $H$ of $G$, then $G$ has a finite $2$-dimensional classifying space $K(G,1)$. The conjecture is related to Wall's D2 Problem and the Relation Gap problem; the pro-$p$ version and higher-dimensional abstract analogues are verified, while the stated discrete conjecture is not resolved here.
record.source_name: Aditi Kar and Nikolay Nikolov, “2D problems in groups”, arXiv:1801.04484 (2018).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1801.04484

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of January 2018).

record.title: Vinogradov's conjecture on the least primitive root
record.statement:
Let $p$ be a prime, and let $g(p)$ denote the least primitive root modulo $p$, equivalently the smallest generator of the multiplicative group of integers modulo $p$.

**Vinogradov's conjecture.** For every $\epsilon>0$, for all sufficiently large primes $p$, one has

$$
g(p)\ll p^{\epsilon}.
$$

This conjecture predicts that the least primitive root grows more slowly than every positive power of $p$. The supplied text does not state whether it has been resolved.
record.source_name: Andrea Sartori, “Least primitive root and simultaneous power-non residues”, arXiv:1801.06110 (2018).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1801.06110

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of January 2018).

record.title: The relative Banzhaf index upper-bound conjecture
record.statement:
Let $w_1,w_2,w_3, \ldots, w_m$ be positive weights, let $w$ be their maximum, and set

$$
N=\sum_{i=1}^{m}w_i.
$$

For a voting game with these weights, let $\beta_i$ denote the relative Banzhaf index of player $i$. **Relative Banzhaf index upper-bound conjecture.** For every player $i$,

$$
\beta_i\leq\frac{2w}{N}.
$$

The authors report that this relation was observed in their calculations for voting games but had not been proved. It is presented as a narrow bound on the relative Banzhaf indices.
record.source_name: Krishna V. Acharya, Himadri Mukherjee and Jajati Keshari Sahoo, “Approximation of Banzhaf indices and its application to voting games”, arXiv:1801.08029 (2020).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1801.08029

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of January 2018).

record.title: Fraenkel–Paterson–Simpson minimum non-equivalent abelian-square conjecture
record.statement:
For a binary linear word of length $n$, let $MNL(n)$ be the minimum number of non-equivalent abelian squares it contains. **Fraenkel–Paterson–Simpson's conjecture.** For every positive integer $n$,

$$
MNL(n)=\lfloor n/4\rfloor.
$$

When $n=4k+3$, the bound is attained only by $a^{2k+1}ba^{2k+1}$ and $(ab)^{2k+1}a$, together with their complements; when $n$ is not congruent to $3$ modulo $4$, the extremal words are obtained by removing $1$, $2$, or $3$ letters from an end. This conjecture concerns the sharp minimum and the equality cases for non-equivalent abelian squares in binary words.
record.source_name: Jamie Simpson, “Solved and unsolved problems about abelian squares”, arXiv:1802.04481 (2018).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1802.04481

Status: **solved** according to the source (as of February 2018). “This was first proved by Fraenkel and Simpson in 1995, with much nicer proofs coming later from Rampersad, Shallit and Wang in 2005, Harju and Nowotka in 2006 and Badkobeh and Crochemore in 2011.”

record.title: Bean–Tannock–Ulfarsson maximal staircase-encoding conjecture
record.statement:
Let $J(\ell,k)$ denote the number of $132$-avoiding permutations of length $\ell$ whose staircase encoding has $k$ nonzero boxes, and let $C_i$ denote the $i^{\text{th}}$ Catalan number. For fixed $\ell$, let $k$ be the largest value such that $J(\ell,k)\ne 0$. **Bean–Tannock–Ulfarsson's conjecture.** If $\ell=3i+2$, then

$$
J(\ell,k)=C_i,
$$

and if $\ell=3i+1$, then

$$
J(\ell,k)=\frac{3}{2}{2i\choose i}.
$$

The paper states that this conjecture is proved using the preceding generating-function theorem and the formula for $J(\ell,k)$, so the conjecture is resolved.
record.source_name: Shyam Narayanan, “Resolving Two Conjectures on Staircase Encodings and Boundary Grids of 132 and 123-avoiding permutations”, arXiv:1802.06345 (2019).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1802.06345

Status: the source reports no resolution (as of February 2018); treated as **open**. (An automated reading suggested “solved”, which the source does not establish — worth checking against the literature.)

record.title: Maximum fluctuation conjecture for halfway permutation paths
record.statement:
Let $sigma^n$ be an $n$-element uniform random sorting network and define

$$
Z_j^n(t)=e^{\pi i t}\left[sigma_G^n(j,t)+isigma_G^n(j,t+1/2)\right].
$$

**Maximum fluctuation conjecture.** For every $epsilon>0$,

$$
\max_{j\in[1,n]}\sup_{s,t\in[0,1]}n^{1/2-epsilon}|Z_j^n(t)-Z_j^n(s)|\to0
$$

in probability as $n\to\infty$. This predicts a uniform upper bound, up to an arbitrary power $n^\epsilon$, on fluctuations of all halfway-permutation paths; the paper presents it as an open problem.
record.source_name: Duncan Dauvergne and Bálint Virág, “Circular support in random sorting networks”, arXiv:1802.08933 (2018).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1802.08933

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of February 2018).

record.title: Equality of the honest-effort and attainable tournament regions
record.statement:
Let $\mathcal{A}_n$ denote the set of score vectors attainable in tournaments on $n$ players, and let $\mathcal{A}^{*}_n$ denote the region generated by the tournament configurations described above. The examples satisfy $\mathcal{A}^{*}_1=\mathcal{A}_1$, $\mathcal{A}^{*}_2=\mathcal{A}_2$, and $\mathcal{A}^{*}_3=\mathcal{A}_3$. **Equality conjecture.**

$$
\mathcal{A}^{*}_n=\mathcal{A}_n,
$$

for every $n\in\mathbb{N}$. This would assert that the configurations captured by $\mathcal{A}^{*}_n$ produce exactly all attainable score vectors, despite the map used to construct the region ceasing to be injective for $n\geq 3$.
record.source_name: Peter Hegarty, Anders Martinsson and Edvin Wedin, “The "No Justice in the Universe" phenomenon: why honesty of effort may not be rewarded in tournaments”, arXiv:1803.00823 (2018).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1803.00823

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of March 2018).

record.title: Quadratic-time partition conjecture for noncomplete connected graphs
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a connected graph with maximum degree $k \geq 3$, distinct from $K_{k+1}$. For integers $s \geq 2$ and $p_1,\ldots,p_s \geq 0$ satisfying

$$
p_1+\cdots+p_s \geq k-s,
$$

a $(p_1,\ldots,p_s)$-partition of $G$ is a partition of $V(G)$ into $s$ parts such that the subgraph induced by the $i$th part has maximum degree at most $p_i$. **Quadratic-time partition conjecture.** For every such $G$, $s$, and $p_1,\ldots,p_s$, a $(p_1,\ldots,p_s)$-partition of $G$ can be found in $O(n^2)$ time. The preceding proposition establishes the corresponding linear-time result when $G$ is not regular; the conjecture concerns the remaining regular case and is presented as an outstanding case in the paper.
record.source_name: Faisal N. Abu-Khzam, Carl Feghali and Pinar Heggernes, “Partitioning a graph into degenerate subgraphs”, arXiv:1803.04388 (2019).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1803.04388

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of March 2018).

record.title: The conjecture for even-clique Ramsey–Turán densities
record.statement:
Let $R(3,s)$ be the smallest integer $N$ such that every red-blue colouring of $K_N$ contains a red $K_3$ or a blue $K_s$. Let $\varrho(K_3,K_{2s})$ denote the multicolour Ramsey–Turán density for triangle versus the even clique $K_{2s}$. **Even-clique Ramsey–Turán conjecture.** For all $s\geq2$,

$$
\varrho(K_3,K_{2s})=\frac{1}{2}\left(1-\frac{1}{R(3,s)}\right).
$$

This is proposed as the even-clique analogue of the previously recalled odd-clique conjecture. The provided text gives no resolution, so the conjecture remains open here.
record.source_name: Jaehoon Kim, Younjin Kim and Hong Liu, “Two conjectures in Ramsey-Turán theory”, arXiv:1803.04721 (2018).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1803.04721

Status: **solved** according to the source (as of March 2018).

record.title: NSSW excluded-configuration conjecture for minor-closed classes
record.statement:
Let $\mathcal{X}_{k,c}$ be the graph family defined in the source, and let $\mathcal{M}$ be a minor-closed class. **NSSW excluded-configuration conjecture.** Every minor-closed class that excludes every graph in $\mathcal{X}_{k,c}$ for some integer $c$ is $k$-colourable with bounded clustering.

Equivalently, for every minor-closed class $\mathcal{M}$, $\chi_{\star}(\mathcal{M})$ should equal the minimum integer $k$ such that $\mathcal{M}\cap\mathcal{X}_{k,c}=\varnothing$ for some integer $c$. The source provides the construction and a rainbow-clique obstruction, but does not establish the conjecture in general.
record.source_name: David R. Wood, “Defective and Clustered Graph Colouring”, arXiv:1803.07694 (2018).
record.references:
**2 papers in this index state this conjecture** (2017–2018). The statement above is taken from the most recent of them; the others are [arXiv:1708.02370](https://arxiv.org/abs/1708.02370).

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1803.07694

Status: **open** according to the source (as of March 2018). “This is widely considered one of the most important open problems in graph theory; see for a survey.”

record.title: The conjectured upper bound for minimum dominating sets in trees
record.statement:
Let $T$ be a finite tree with domination number $gamma$, and let a minimum dominating set be a dominating set of cardinality $gamma$. The number of minimum dominating sets of $T$ is at most

$$
O\left(\frac{gamma 2^{gamma}}{\ln gamma}\right).
$$

**Upper-bound conjecture.** A tree with domination number $\gamma$ has at most $O\left(\frac{\gamma 2^{\gamma}}{\ln \gamma}\right)$ minimum dominating sets. The conjecture refines the previously considered $2^\gamma$ bound, which is false for all trees but is believed to capture the correct exponential growth rate.
record.source_name: J. D. Alvarado, S. Dantas, E. Mohr and D. Rautenbach, “On the maximum number of minimum dominating sets in forests”, arXiv:1804.00158 (2018).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1804.00158

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of April 2018).

record.title: Uniform integrability conjecture for graphs with smallest eigenvalue at least -3
record.statement: Let $G$ be a connected graph, and let its smallest eigenvalue be denoted by $4\lambda_{\min}(G)4$. A graph is **$\sigma$-integrable** if its associated integral lattice admits an embedding, after scaling the bilinear form by $\sigma$, into a standard integer lattice. **Uniform integrability conjecture.** There exists a positive integer $\sigma$ such that any connected graph $G$ with smallest eigenvalue at least $-3$ is $\sigma$-integrable. This conjecture asks for a uniform integrability bound for all connected graphs whose smallest eigenvalue is at least $-3$; the preceding results establish integrability in important cases, but the existence of one universal positive integer remains open.
record.source_name: Jack H. Koolen, Jae Young Yang and Qianqian Yang, “On graphs with smallest eigenvalue at least -3 and their lattices”, arXiv:1804.00369 (2018).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1804.00369

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of April 2018).

record.title: The asymptotic number of copies of $\wedge_s$ in $\{\wedge_k,\vee_l\}$-free families
record.statement:
Let $\wedge_r$ be the poset on elements $a,b_1,\ldots,b_r$ with $a<b_i$ for every $i$, and let $\vee_r$ be its dual. For a family of posets $\mathcal P$ and a poset $Q$, let $La(n,\mathcal P,Q)$ denote the maximum number of copies of $Q$ in a $\mathcal P$-free family ${\mathcal F}\subseteq 2^{[n]}$. **The sharp lower-bound conjecture.** For any integers $k,l,s$ with $s\le k-1$,

$$
La(n,\{\wedge_k,\vee_l\},\wedge_s)=\left(\binom{k-1}{s}\frac{l-1}{k+l-2}+o(1)\right)\binom{n}{\lfloor n/2\rfloor}.
$$

The paper proves the same expression as a lower bound by generalizing a construction of Katona and Tarján, and conjectures that this lower bound is sharp.
record.source_name: Dániel Gerbner, Abhishek Methuku, Dániel T. Nagy, Balázs Patkós and Máté Vizer, “On the number of containments in P-free families”, arXiv:1804.01606 (2018).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1804.01606

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of April 2018).

record.title: The first threshold conjecture for unbounded indecomposable permutations
record.statement:
Let $\mathcal{C}$ be a sum-closed permutation class, and let $\mathcal{C}^{\not\oplus}$ denote its indecomposable permutations. Define $\tau$ to be the unique positive root of

$$
x^3-3x^2+2x-1=0,
$$

so that $\tau\approx 2.32472$. **First threshold conjecture.** If $|\mathcal{C}^{\not\oplus}_n|$ is unbounded, then

$$
\operatorname{gr}(\mathcal{C})\geq\tau;
$$

in other words, $\tau$ is the smallest possible growth rate of a sum-closed class with unbounded numbers of indecomposable permutations. The class $\operatorname{Av}(321,3142,2413)$ realizes growth rate $\tau$, while the paper establishes that the threshold is at least $\xi\approx2.30522$; determining whether no smaller value than $\tau$ is possible remains open.
record.source_name: Justin M. Troyka, “On the centrosymmetric permutations in a class”, arXiv:1804.03686 (2019).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1804.03686

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of April 2018).

record.title: The Bernardi-process conjecture for determining ribbon-graph genus
record.statement:
Let $(G,\rho)$ be a ribbon graph. Write $V(G)$ for its vertices, $E(G)$ for its edges, $\operatorname{Pic}^0(G)$ for its degree-zero Picard group, and $\mathcal{T}(G)\subset E(G)$ for its spanning trees. For every $v\in V(G)$, suppose we are given the map

$$
\operatorname{Pic}^0(G)\times\mathcal{T}(G)\xrightarrow{\beta_v(\operatorname{Pic}^0(G))}\mathcal{T}(G),
$$

where $\beta_v$ is the Bernardi process with basepoint $v$. **Bernardi-process conjecture.** It is possible to determine the genus of $(G,\rho)$ from this data. The challenge is that, even for a cut-free graph, the Bernardi process does not readily detect the cyclic order around a fixed vertex without information about the cyclic orders around other vertices.
record.source_name: Alex McDonough, “Determining Genus From Sandpile Torsor Algorithms”, arXiv:1804.07807 (2021).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1804.07807

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of April 2018).

record.title: BCFW triangulation conjecture for amplituhedra in four dimensions
record.statement: For $m=4$, let $\mathcal{T}_{k,\ell}=\{f_1,\dots,f_N\}$ be the BCFW collection of positroid cells, with $\mathcal{T}_{\ell,k}=\{f_1^{-1},\dots,f_N^{-1}\}$ up to cyclic shift. **BCFW triangulation conjecture.** For every $k$ and $\ell$, $\mathcal{T}_{k,\ell}$ is an $(n,k,m)$-triangulation of degree $1$. The BCFW collection is widely used to compute the amplituhedron form; the source gives no general proof.
record.source_name: Pavel Galashin and Thomas Lam, “Parity duality for the amplituhedron”, arXiv:1805.00600 (2018).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1805.00600

Status: **open** according to the source (as of May 2018). “It is an important open problem to give a formula for $\omega_{\ampl}$ without referring to triangulations.”

record.title: Universal CW-cell conjecture for the two-number of compact symmetric spaces
record.statement: Let $M$ be a connected compact symmetric space, let $\#_2M$ denote its two-number, and let a CW complex structure on $M$ be a cellular decomposition of $M$. **Universal CW-cell conjecture.** For every connected compact symmetric space $M$, $\#_2M$ is equal to the smallest number of cells needed for a CW complex structure on $M$. This is the third conjecture in the source's list and is recorded there as open. It extends the earlier formulation involving connected compact symmetric spaces by making the universal quantifier explicit.
record.source_name: Bang-Yen Chen, “Two-numbers and their applications - A survey”, arXiv:1805.04796 (2018).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1805.04796

Status: **open** according to the source (as of May 2018). “These 3 conjectures remain open till now.”

record.title: Super-linear edge-statistics conjecture
record.statement:
Let $\operatorname{ind}(k,\ell)$ denote the limiting maximum proportion of $k$-vertex subsets inducing exactly $\ell$ edges. **Super-linear edge-statistics conjecture.** For all pairs $(k,\ell)$ satisfying

$$
\min \left\{\ell, \binom{k}{2} - \ell \right\} = \omega(k),
$$

we have

$$
\operatorname{ind}(k,\ell) = o(1).
$$

The paper proves the analogous assertion when both edge counts are quadratic in $k$ and proposes replacing “quadratic” by “super-linear.” This strengthening remains open.
record.source_name: Noga Alon, Dan Hefetz, Michael Krivelevich and Mykhaylo Tyomkyn, “Edge-statistics on large graphs”, arXiv:1805.06848 (2019).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1805.06848

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of May 2018).

record.title: The large-convex-combination conjecture for non-vertex integer partitions
record.statement: Let $P_n$ be the convex hull of the integer partitions of $n$. For a non-vertex partition $x\in P(n)$, let $\xi(x)$ be the minimum number of partitions of $n$ needed to express $x$ as a convex combination of other partitions, and let $C_\xi(n)$ be the set of partitions $x$ with $\xi(x)=\xi$. **The non-vertex representation conjecture.** For every $\xi$, the set $C_\xi(n)$ is nonempty for all sufficiently large $n>n_0(\xi)$; for every $n$, the cardinality $|C_\xi(n)|$ decreases as $\xi$ grows. The paper establishes nonemptiness for some small values of $\xi$ and leaves the general assertion open.
record.source_name: Vladimir A. Shlyk, “Number of Vertices of the Polytope of Integer Partitions and Factorization of the Partitioned Number”, arXiv:1805.07989 (2018).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1805.07989

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of May 2018).

record.title: Stable-center single-cycle generation conjecture
record.statement:
Let $q$ be a prime power, let $
\Phi$ be the set of monic irreducible polynomials over $
\mathbb F_q$ other than $t$, and let $
\mathscr{G}(q)$ be the stable graded algebra with single cycle class sums $K_{(r)_f}$ indexed by $r\geq 1$ and $f\in\Phi$. 

**Stable-center generation conjecture.** The stable center

$$
\mathbb Q\otimes_{\mathbb Z}\mathscr{G}(q)
$$

is the polynomial algebra generated by the single cycle class sums $K_{(r)_f}$, for all $r\geq 1$ and $f\in\Phi$.

This conjecture gives an explicit polynomial description of the stable center in terms of elementary cycle classes. The source provides no resolution or further evidence sufficient to determine its status.

record.title: Finite-bound conjecture for independent three-variable word-equation systems
record.statement: Let a **system of equations** be a set of word equations, and call it **independent** if it is not equivalent to any proper subset. A system is **constant-free** when its equations contain only variables, and a solution is **nonperiodic** when it is not periodic. Consider independent systems of constant-free equations in three variables having a nonperiodic solution. **Finite-bound conjecture.** There exists a number $c$ such that every such system has size at most $c$. This is explicitly presented as a weaker conjecture than the claim that the largest examples have size two. The paper proves a bound of $17$, while the conjectured bound of two remains open; consequently, the existence of some finite bound is open in the source's stated context.
record.source_name: Dirk Nowotka and Aleksi Saarela, “An optimal bound on the solution sets of one-variable word equations and its consequences”, arXiv:1805.09535 (2018).

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1805.09535

record.title: Generalised Catalan conjecture for largest binary tropical matrix equivalence classes
record.statement:
Let $W(\ell_a,\ell_a)$ be the set of binary words containing $\ell_a$ occurrences of each letter, and consider its $\mathcal{UT}_2(\mathbb{T})$ equivalence classes. **Generalised Catalan conjecture.** For each fixed $\ell_a\geq 5$, the largest equivalence class in $W(\ell_a,\ell_a)$ belongs to the generalised Catalan family defined in the source.

The conjecture concerns the extremal structure of equivalence classes with balanced letter content. It has been verified numerically by exhaustive enumeration through words of length $24$, but no general proof is supplied.
record.source_name: Marianne Johnson and Ngoc Mai Tran, “Geometry and algorithms for upper triangular tropical matrix identities”, arXiv:1806.01835 (2018).

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1806.01835

record.title: Intermediate matching number conjecture for tree degree sequences
record.statement:
Let $\mathbf{s}$ be a tree degree sequence of length $n>2$, and let $\mathcal{T}_{\mathbf{s}}$ denote the trees with degree sequence $\mathbf{s}$. Write $\nu_m(\mathcal{T}_{\mathbf{s}})$ and $\nu_M(\mathcal{T}_{\mathbf{s}})$ for the minimum and maximum matching numbers among these trees.

**Intermediate matching number conjecture.** For every positive integer $k$ satisfying

$$
\nu_m(\mathcal{T}_{\mathbf{s}})\leq k\leq\nu_M(\mathcal{T}_{\mathbf{s}}),
$$

there exists a tree $T\in\mathcal{T}_{\mathbf{s}}$ such that $\nu(T)=k$.

This asserts that the matching numbers realized by trees with a fixed degree sequence contain every integer between the minimum and maximum values. The supplied text gives no evidence of resolution.
record.source_name: Gonzalo Molina and Daniel A. Jaume, “Maximum and minimum nullity of a tree degree sequence”, arXiv:1806.02399 (2018).

record.title: Large monochromatic component conjecture for dense bipartite graphs
record.statement:
Let $r\geq 3$ and let $G$ be an $(X,Y)$-bipartite graph with $|X|=m$ and $|Y|=n$. Write $\delta(X,Y)$ and $\delta(Y,X)$ for the minimum degrees from $X$ into $Y$ and from $Y$ into $X$, respectively.

**Dense bipartite component conjecture.** If

$$
\delta(X,Y) > \left( 1 - \frac{1}{r+1}\right) n
$$

and

$$
\delta(Y,X) > \left( 1 - \frac{1}{r+1}\right) m,
$$

then every $r$-edge coloring of $G$ has a monochromatic component on at least

$$
\frac{m+n}{r}
$$

vertices.

This conjecture extends the corresponding result for complete bipartite graphs and the proved two-color case to arbitrary numbers of colors; the source states a weaker theorem as the best result currently available.
record.source_name: Louis DeBiasio, Robert A. Krueger and Gábor N. Sárközy, “Large monochromatic components in multicolored bipartite graphs”, arXiv:1806.05271 (2019).

record.title: Square-root recurrence conjecture for extremal reciprocal algebraic integers
record.statement:
Let $\mathrm{mr}(d)$ be the minimum of the houses of reciprocal algebraic integers of degree $d$ that are not roots of unity. An algebraic integer attaining $\mathrm{mr}(d)$ is called **extremal reciprocal**. If its minimal polynomial is denoted by $R_d(x)$, then, for even $d\geq 8$, **the square-root recurrence conjecture** states that an extremal reciprocal $\alpha$ of degree $d$ gives an extremal reciprocal $\sqrt{\alpha}$ of degree $2d$, with

$$
R_{2d}(x)=R_d(x^2).
$$

The claim is suggested by computations through even degree $34$ and describes a recurrence for the extremal reciprocal polynomials. No resolution status is given in the source.
record.source_name: Dragan Stankov, “The House of a Reciprocal Algebraic Integer”, arXiv:1806.06424 (2018).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1806.06424

record.title: Prime-degree extremal polynomial conjecture in the 5 modulo 6 case
record.statement:
Let $d\geq 17$ be prime with $d\equiv 5\pmod 6$. Define

$$
P_d(x)=\frac{x^{d+2}-x^2-1}{x^2-x+1}.
$$

Let an algebraic integer of degree $d$ that is not a root of unity be **extremal** if it has the minimum possible house among such algebraic integers. **Prime-degree extremal polynomial conjecture.** The extremal $\alpha$ has minimal polynomial $P_d(x)$.

The polynomial is established in the source to have a real root between $1$ and $\sqrt[d]{2}$, with its $d$th power tending to $2$; computations for $d=17$ and $23$ motivate the conjecture. No resolution status is given.
record.source_name: Dragan Stankov, “The House of a Reciprocal Algebraic Integer”, arXiv:1806.06424 (2018).

record.title: Conjecture on the generators of the abelianisation of Gamma_n(1,n/2-1)
record.statement:
Let $\Gamma_n(1,n/2-1)$ be the cyclically presented group in the source, let $\Gamma_n(1,n/2-1)^\mathrm{ab}$ denote its abelianisation, and let $d(G)$ be the minimum number of generators of a finite abelian group $G$. **Generator-number conjecture.** Suppose $(n,6)=2$ and $n\geq 8$. Then

$$
d(\Gamma_n(1,n/2-1)^\mathrm{ab})=\begin{cases}1&\mathrm{if}~(n,16)=2,\\2&\mathrm{if}~(n,16)=4~\mathrm{or}~16,\\3&\mathrm{if}~(n,16)=8.\end{cases}
$$

The conjecture was verified computationally using GAP for $n\leq 500$; the paper notes that the third case also has an established lower bound of three, while the remaining cases are not proved there.
record.source_name: Esamaldeen Mohamed and Gerald Williams, “An investigation into the cyclically presented groups with length three positive relators”, arXiv:1806.06821 (2019).

record.title: Koumandos–Ruscheweyh weaker conjecture for partial sums
record.statement:
Let $s_n^{\mu}(z)=\displaystyle\sum_{k=0}^n \frac{(\mu)_k}{k!}z^k$ for $0<\mu\leq1$, and let $\rho\in(0,1]$. Let $\mu^{\ast}(\rho)$ be the number defined by

$$
\int_{0}^{(\rho+1)\pi}\frac{\sin(t-\rho\pi)}{t^{1-\mu}}dt=0.
$$

**Koumandos–Ruscheweyh weaker conjecture.** For every $z\in\mathbb{D}$, $n\in\mathbb{N}$, and $0<\mu\leq\mu^{\ast}(\rho)$,

$$
\operatorname{Re}\left((1-z)^{2\rho-1}s_n^{\mu}(z)\right)>0.
$$

Moreover, $\mu^{\ast}(\rho)$ is the largest number with this property. This is presented as a weaker form of the preceding subordination conjecture, and the supplied text gives no resolution status.
record.source_name: Priyanka Sangal and A. Swaminathan, “On a conjecture for trigonometric sums by S. Koumandos and S. Ruscheweyh”, arXiv:1806.06999 (2018).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1806.06999

Status: **solved** according to the source (as of June 2018). “Since both the conjectures hold good for the harmonic mean of $1/2$ \& $1/4$ and $1/2$ \& $1$, affirmative solution to the following conjecture will settle both these conjectures.”

record.title: Conjectured asymptotics for the Subgraph Query Problem on cliques
record.statement:
For $p\in(0,1)$, let $f(H,p)$ be the minimum number of turns, over Builder strategies, needed to build a copy of $H$ with probability at least $1/2$ when each queried edge succeeds independently with probability $p$. **Subgraph Query conjecture.** For every $m\ge4$,

$$
f(K_m,p)=2^{o(m)}p^{-\frac{2}{3}m+c_m},
$$

where

$$
c_m=\begin{cases}\frac{m}{2m-3}&m\equiv0\pmod3,\\frac{2}{3}&m\equiv1\pmod3,\\frac{2m+8}{6m-3}&m\equiv2\pmod3.\end{cases}
$$

The paper proves the corresponding upper bound and proposes that the displayed estimate gives the correct order for finding cliques in the Subgraph Query Game.
record.source_name: David Conlon, Jacob Fox, Andrey Grinshpun and Xiaoyu He, “Online Ramsey Numbers and the Subgraph Query Problem”, arXiv:1806.09726 (2018).

record.title: Farb's conjecture on sections of configuration-space bundles over cubic plane curves
record.statement:
Let $\mathcal{X}$ be the parameter space of smooth cubic plane curves in $\mathbb{C}P^2$ up to nonzero scalar multiplication. For each positive integer $n$, let $\xi_n$ be the fiber bundle over $\mathcal{X}$ whose fiber over a curve is the configuration space of $n$ distinct unordered points on that curve.

**Farb's conjecture.** The smallest value of $n$ for which $\xi_n$ admits a continuous section is

$$
n=9.
$$

Classical constructions provide continuous sections for $n=9$ and for many larger values, including $27$, $36$, and $72$. The conjecture asserts that no continuous section exists for any positive integer $n<9$.
record.source_name: Weiyan Chen, “Obstructions to choosing distinct points on cubic plane curves”, arXiv:1806.10207 (2018).

record.title: The $(4\frac14,\frac14)$-flow conjecture for simple cubic graphs
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a simple cubic graph, and let $bed(G)$ denote the set of flow parameters admitted by $G$ in the source. **$(4\frac14,\frac14)$-flow conjecture.** For every simple cubic graph $G$, 
$$
(4\frac14,\frac14)\in bed(G).
$$
 The claim concerns a uniform flow parameter for simple cubic graphs; the source reports supporting analysis for a smallest example but does not state that the conjecture has been resolved.

record.title: Largest-denominator conjecture for semiqueens
record.statement:
Let $F_k$ be the Fibonacci numbers, and let $\mathbb Q^{21}$ denote the semiqueen. For $q$ semiqueens, consider all vertices of the associated inside-out polytope. **Semiqueen maximal-denominator conjecture.** The largest denominator of a vertex for $q$ semiqueens $\mathbb Q^{21}$ is

$$
F_{\lfloor q/2\rfloor}
$$

if $q$ is even and

$$
F_{\lfloor q/2\rfloor+1}-1
$$

if $q$ is odd. This is presented as the specialization of the general three-move maximality conjecture to semiqueens.
record.source_name: Seth Chaiken, Christopher R. H. Hanusa and Thomas Zaslavsky, “A q-Queens Problem. IV. Attacking Configurations and Their Denominators”, arXiv:1807.04741 (2018).

record.title: The edge b1-critical graph conjecture on disjoint maximum independent sets
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a graph. It is **edge $\alpha$-critical** if $\alpha(G-e)>\alpha(G)$ for every $e\in E(G)$; an independent set is **maximum** if it has cardinality $\alpha(G)$, and $G$ has **two disjoint maximum independent sets** if there are $A,B\subseteq V(G)$ with $A\cap B=\varnothing$ and $|A|=|B|=\alpha(G)$. **The edge $\alpha$-critical graph conjecture.** If $G$ is an edge $\alpha$-critical graph without isolated vertices, then it has two disjoint maximum independent sets.

This conjecture extends the examples of odd cycles and their complements, which are edge $\alpha$-critical and have two disjoint maximum independent sets. Its resolution is not supplied in the source.
record.source_name: Zakir Deniz, Vadim E. Levit and Eugen Mandrescu, “On graphs admitting two disjoint maximum independent sets”, arXiv:1807.06914 (2019).

record.title: The perfect-matching covering conjecture for claw-free bridgeless cubic graphs
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a claw-free bridgeless cubic graph, and let $k(G)$ be the smallest number of perfect matchings needed to cover the edge-set of $G$.

**Claw-free Berge conjecture.** For every claw-free bridgeless cubic graph $G$,

$$
k(G)\leq 4.
$$

This strengthens Berge's bound from five to four on claw-free bridgeless cubic graphs. The source presents it as a suspicion and uses it in connection with the $(5,2)$-even-subgraph-cover conjecture.
record.source_name: Anush Hakobyan and Vahan Mkrtchyan, “S_12 and P_12-colorings of cubic graphs”, arXiv:1807.08138 (2018).

record.title: The $P_{12}$-coloring conjecture for cubic graphs covered by four perfect matchings
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a cubic graph, and let $k(G)$ be the smallest number of perfect matchings needed to cover its edge-set. Write $P_{12}\prec G$ when $G$ admits a $P_{12}$-coloring.

**$P_{12}$-coloring conjecture.** Every cubic graph $G$ with $k(G)\leq 4$ admits a $P_{12}$-coloring:

$$
P_{12}\prec G.
$$

Equivalently, the edge-set of $G$ can be covered by four perfect matchings. The conjecture is one of the paper's two new coloring conjectures and is used to relate covering problems to the Petersen coloring conjecture.

record.title: Strict diameter-based eigenvalue bound for non-tree quantum graphs
record.statement:
Let $\mathcal{G}$ be any connected, compact graph with total length $L$ and diameter $D$, and let $\mu_k(\mathcal{G})$ denote its $k$-th eigenvalue. Assume that $L/k>D/2$. **Strict diameter-based eigenvalue conjecture.** Then $\mu_k(\mathcal{G})$ is strictly larger than the square of the smallest positive solution $\omega>0$ of

$$
\cos\left(\frac{\omega D}{2}\right)=\omega\left(\frac{L}{k}-\frac{D}{2}\right)\sin\left(\frac{\omega D}{2}\right).
$$

The conjecture proposes a sharper form of the preceding diameter-based bound, removing the cycle-rank term and the assumption excluding long loops. The cited examples of loops and tadpoles motivate the claim, while its validity for arbitrary connected compact graphs remains open.
record.source_name: J. B. Kennedy, “A family of diameter-based eigenvalue bounds for quantum graphs”, arXiv:1807.08185 (2019).

record.title: The odd-genus Penner dilatation limit conjecture
record.statement:
Let $N_g$ be the nonorientable closed surface of genus $g$, and let $delta_P(N_g)$ denote the minimal dilatation among pseudo-Anosov homeomorphisms arising from Penner's construction on $N_g$. The odd-genus limit is

$$
\lim_{k\to\infty}\delta_P(N_{2k+1}).
$$

**Odd-genus Penner dilatation limit conjecture.** The limit is the largest real root of

$$
x^4-8x^3+13x^2-8x+1,
$$

approximately $6.071360241468951$. The preceding theorem establishes only that this limit exists and is greater than $3+2\sqrt{2}$; the stated value is suggested by computations and remains open.
record.source_name: Livio Liechti and Balázs Strenner, “Minimal Penner dilatations on nonorientable surfaces”, arXiv:1807.08940 (2023).

record.title: The low-point Mori dream space conjecture for Hirzebruch-surface Hilbert schemes
record.statement:
Let $\mathbb{F}_r$ be the $r$th Hirzebruch surface, and let $\mathbb{F}_r^{[r-k]}$ denote its Hilbert scheme of $r-k$ points, where $r>k\geq 0$. Write $\overline{\operatorname{Eff}}(\mathbb{F}_r^{[r-k]})$ for its pseudo-effective cone.

**Low-point Mori dream space conjecture.** The Hilbert scheme $\mathbb{F}_r^{[r-k]}$ is a Mori dream space, and the decomposition of $\overline{\operatorname{Eff}}(\mathbb{F}_r^{[r-k]})$ is given by the walls defined in Theorem 4.15 of BC13.

This conjecture gives a partial converse to the preceding wall-inheritance proposition when the number of points is low compared with $r$. The cited wall description is intended to determine the full decomposition of the effective cone.
record.source_name: Cesar Lozano Huerta and Tim Ryan, “On the birational geometry of Hilbert schemes of points and Severi divisors”, arXiv:1807.09881 (2019).

record.title: The spider lower-bound equality conjecture for maximum rectilinear crossing numbers
record.statement:
Let $S$ be a spider with $k\geq 3$ legs, whose lengths satisfy

$$
\ell_1\geq \ell_2\geq \cdots \geq \ell_k.
$$

Let $\vartheta(S)$ denote the thrackle bound, and let $\max\text{-}\overline{\operatorname{cr}}(S)$ denote the maximum rectilinear crossing number of $S$.

**Spider lower-bound conjecture.**

$$
\max\text{-}\overline{\operatorname{cr}}(S)=\vartheta(S)-\sum_{i=3}^k(\ell_i-1)\left\lfloor\frac{i-1}{2}\right\rfloor.
$$

The formula asserts that the lower bound obtained from the paper's drawing algorithm is exact for every spider. The authors motivate it by noting that the upper and lower bounds agree when all legs have length two, while their method does not otherwise generalize; the supplied text gives no resolution of the general conjecture.
record.source_name: Joshua Fallon, Kirsten Hogenson, Lauren Keough, Mario Lomelí, Marcus Schaefer and Pablo Soberón, “A Note on the Maximum Rectilinear Crossing Number of Spiders”, arXiv:1808.00385 (2021).

record.title: Füredi's higher-dimensional Erdős–Szekeres conjecture
record.statement:
Let $ES_d(n)$ be the minimum integer $N$ such that every set of $N$ points in $\mathbb{R}^d$ in general position contains $n$ points in convex position. **Füredi's conjecture.** For every $d\geq 3$, 

$$
ES_d(n)=2^{\Theta\left(n^{1/(d-1)}\right)}.
$$

This conjecture predicts that the known lower bound for the higher-dimensional Erdős–Szekeres problem is asymptotically sharp. The upper bound $ES_d(n)\leq 2^{n+o(n)}$ is known, while the matching upper bound of order $2^{O(n^{1/(d-1)})}$ remains open.
record.source_name: Dhruv Mubayi and Andrew Suk, “The Erdos-Szekeres problem and an induced Ramsey question”, arXiv:1808.00453 (2018).

record.title: Second-eigenvalue conjecture for the auxiliary graph $FJ_1(n,2)$
record.statement:
For $n\geq 4$, let $FJ_1(n,2)=\mathrm{Cay}(S_n,RP_1^{(2)})$ be the connected auxiliary Cayley graph defined in the source, and let $B_n^{(1)}$ be its displayed quotient matrix. Write $\lambda_2$ for the second-largest adjacency eigenvalue. **The $FJ_1(n,2)$ quotient-matrix conjecture.**

$$
\lambda_2(FJ_1(n,2))=\lambda_2(B_n^{(1)}).
$$

The equality is verified computationally in the source for $4\leq n\leq 7$. The conjecture asks whether the second adjacency eigenvalue of this auxiliary graph is equal to that of its quotient matrix for all $n\geq 4$.
